claims.text: Nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution catalysts catalyze ethanol oxidation through a 12-electron process.
PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts exhibit exceptional selectivity toward complete ethanol oxidation.
Complete ethanol oxidation is a 12-electron process that produces CO2.
The selectivity of PtPdRhRuIrOs is governed by a broad distribution of adsorption energies created by lattice strain and ligand effects.
Strong-binding surface sites promote adsorption and dehydrogenation of ethanol-derived species.
Weak-binding surface sites facilitate further oxidation of carbonaceous intermediates to CO2.
Neighboring active sites with different local electronic structures in high-entropy alloys can tune selectivity in complex reactions.
The as-synthesized PtPdRhRuIrOs nanoparticles have high lattice strain.
The as-synthesized PtPdRhRuIrOs nanoparticles have a homogeneous elemental distribution.
A homogeneous elemental distribution promotes a broad range of adsorption energies.
Lattice distortions create a Gaussian-like distribution of adsorption energies in the as-synthesized catalyst.
Mild annealing can reduce lattice strain without causing elemental segregation or significant particle growth.
Reducing lattice strain will narrow the adsorption-energy distribution.
Narrowing the adsorption-energy distribution will reduce the abundance of sites optimized for the 12-electron pathway.
Reducing lattice strain will shift ethanol oxidation toward a four-electron pathway.
Single constituent metals generally promote no more than a four-electron ethanol-oxidation process.
Relative to the as-synthesized catalyst, the strain-reduced annealed catalyst will produce CO2 at a lower rate.
Relative to the as-synthesized catalyst, the strain-reduced annealed catalyst will yield more acetaldehyde or acetic acid.
The prediction is limited to annealing that reduces strain without sintering, phase segregation, or significant changes in surface oxidation state.
Changes in surface oxidation state may independently influence the ethanol-oxidation pathway.
